Project Summary
The Rio Metro Regional Transit District is pleased 
to announce the upcoming implementation of the 
Operation and Maintenance Facility (OMF). The OMF 
will replace the Rail Runner’s existing 1960’s-era freight 
facility, updating it with modern, efficient, state-of-the-art 
equipment to meet or exceed passenger rail industry 
standards across the nation. Once complete, the effort 
will significantly improve working conditions, reduce 
maintenance and repair costs, support well-paying jobs, 
and expand the resiliency and reliability of the Rail 
Runner. 
Why Are Improvements Needed?
Since the Rail Runners expansion to Santa Fe 
(December 2008), Rio Metro has maintained 31 Rail 
Runner locomotives and railcars in an open-air facility 
and out dated buildings that date to the mid-1900s. 
This created conditions in which crews maintaining Rail 
Runner locomotives are often working in unfavorable 
conditions. This includes working in single and triple digit 
temperatures, ice and snow, blowing dust, thunderstorms 
and other inclement weather conditions. Additionally, 
with much of current maintenance being conducted 
outdoors, noise and emissions from maintenance 
potentially impacts surrounding neighborhoods.   
The OMF construction will negate these and other 
conditions that compromise workplace safety and 
service efficiency, while also reducing environmental 
impacts on site and to surrounding neighborhoods, in 
addition, the OMF will support well-paying jobs, and 
enabling the future expansion of commuter rail service. 
Project Details
Located near Downtown Albuquerque, NM, the 
centerpiece of the OMF construction includes a two-
story maintenance shop equipped with a high-bay shop, 
parts storeroom, work and storage areas, and offices.

Strategic Goals
The OMF will be designed to meet the US Department of Transportation strategic goals.  This includes improvements 
or benefits to the following:
 SAFETY
	
Î Lower risk of slips, trips and falls, and exposure to extreme temperatures
	
Î Reduced parts contamination from moisture, blowing dust, exterior storage
	
Î Integrated heavy machinery, fall protection, and platforms
	
Î Improved lighting levels for inspections
	
Î Increased security and prevention of trespassing
ECONOMIC STRENGTH AND GLOBAL COMPETITIVENESS
	
Î Supports prevailing-wage construction jobs
	
Î Mechanical crew pay exceed NM’s median household income
	
Î Ideally located to minimize train deadhead and maximize past infrastructure investments
EQUITY
	
Î Located in a historically disadvantaged community and area of persistent poverty
	
Î Reduced noise and light pollution, as well as locomotive emissions to neighborhoods in 95th-percentile for diesel 
particulate matter
	
Î ADA-compliant improvements to surrounding streets
CLIMATE AND SUSTAINABILITY
	
Î 50 percent reduction in train movements reduces emissions/increases service efficiency
	
Î Improved stormwater/water quality infrastructure
	
Î Indoor storage of lubricants and fluids, fixed fueling infrastructure, and improved spill protection
TRANSFORMATION
	
Î Able to support future Rail Runner service increases
	
Î Up to two-thirds less time to perform major repairs
	
Î Rio Metro intends to pursue LEED certification
	
Î Additional information regarding the OMF will be available as the project design advances.
Funding
In 2024, Rio Metro requested and was awarded $22.5 
million from the federal RAISE grant program helping to 
begin initial efforts regarding the design and development 
of the OMF. Rio Metro is actively pursuing additional 
funding opportunities to complete the design and 
construction of this project. Design is anticipated to last 
approximately 1.5 years and be immediately followed by 
two years of construction.
